qAndA.answer: The manubrium (top), body (middle), and xiphoid process (bottom).
qAndA.question: What are the three main parts of the sternum?
What is the name of the notch located at the very top center of the sternum?
What type of cartilage connects the ribs to the sternum?

qAndA.answer: The sternal angle is the junction between the manubrium and the body of the sternum.
qAndA.question: What is the sternal angle?

narrativeProgression.description: The instructor presents the sternum, then identifies and explains its three main parts: manubrium, body, and xiphoid process. The instructor then points out key landmarks on the manubrium, including the jugular notch, clavicular notches, and sternal angle. Finally, the instructor mentions the costal cartilage.

text_to_speech: Okay so now we're looking at the sternum. So on our sternum you've got three sections of it the manubrium is this top part, the body the long part in the middle and the xiphoid process is here at the bottom kind of the pointier part of your bone at the bottom okay the manubrium is separated from the body by the sternal angle. Okay you have notches here at the top so the one in the middle is our jugular notch and then on either side is our clavicular notches its where the clavicle comes in and articulates with it. You can also see all these things on the sides these are not ribs they're cartilage called the costal cartilage.
